page: Microsoft Azure M416-208ms_v2 is an ultra-high-memory instance belonging to the MSv2 family. It is powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors running at 2.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The server provides 208 dedicated vCPUs across 104 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint reaches 11,400 GB, translating to 54.81 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage includes 8,796 GB of local SSD capacity, while no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant parallelism alongside high aggregate memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (187,869.4), PassMark CPU score (85,859.16), and PassMark CPU extended instructions (168,400.61). Memory bandwidth reaches 10,444.18 GB/sec on small cached blocks, while uncached 256 MB reads and writes measure 581.2 GB/sec and 305.41 GB/sec respectively. Redis performance reaches 159.37 million SET operations per second, ranking in the top tier.

Single-core performance reflects a noticeable tradeoff, falling into the bottom 25% across stress-ng single-core (1371.19), Geekbench single-core (1122.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (22.44 GB/sec). Consequently, this server is engineered for heavy scale-up concurrency rather than single-threaded latency. From a resource perspective, it concentrates massive memory density and massive multi-threaded capacity into a single instance.

Due to its 11.4 TB memory capacity, high local SSD storage, and extensive multi-core scale, Microsoft Azure M416-208ms_v2 is suited for large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive cache layers, heavy in-memory data analytics, and large multi-threaded compilation workloads.
